questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) What is an information system? (1 mark)

(b) State and briefly explain the 5 basic components of an information system. (2 marks)

(c) Describe the Geographic Information System and explain one example of its application. (3 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Information system (1 mark).** An information system is an organised combination of **people, hardware, software, data and procedures** that collects, processes, stores and distributes information to support the operations, decision making and control of an organisation.

**(b) The 5 basic components (2 marks).**

| Component | Brief explanation |
|---|---|
| Hardware | The physical devices used to input, process, store and output data (computers, scanners, printers, servers). |
| Software | The programs that instruct the hardware: system software (operating system) and application software (database, spreadsheet, payroll package). |
| Data | The raw facts and figures that are entered, stored and processed to produce useful information. |
| People | The users, operators, analysts and managers who run the system and use its output. |
| Procedures | The rules, instructions and policies that say how the system is used (data entry rules, backup procedure, security rules). |

(A network or communication component is accepted by some marking schemes in place of procedures.)

**(c) Geographic Information System (GIS) (3 marks).** A GIS is a computer-based system used to **capture, store, analyse, manage and display geographically referenced (spatial) data**. Data are organised in layers (roads, rivers, buildings, population) that are placed on a map so that patterns and relationships between places can be seen and queried.

*One example of application:* **town planning and land management**. A council in a Cameroonian city (for example Douala) can overlay layers of roads, water pipes, flood zones and land plots to choose where to build a new school or market, to find areas at risk of flooding and to plan the routes of water and electricity networks. (Other accepted examples: mapping the spread of a disease such as cholera, tracking delivery vehicles with GPS, locating farms and roads for agriculture, planning emergency response.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
Define the following terms.

(a) Encryption. (2 marks)

(b) Prototype. (2 marks)

(c) Firewall. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Encryption (2 marks).** Encryption is the process of **converting readable data (plaintext) into an unreadable coded form (ciphertext)** using an algorithm and a key, so that only a person who has the correct key can decrypt it and read it. It protects data stored on a computer or sent over a network (for example passwords, online payments).

**(b) Prototype (2 marks).** A prototype is an **early working model (a trial version) of a system or of part of a system**, built quickly during systems development so that users can try it, comment on it and ask for changes before the final system is built. It reduces the risk of building a system that does not meet the users' needs.

**(c) Firewall (2 marks).** A firewall is **hardware or software that monitors and filters the traffic entering and leaving a computer or a network**, according to a set of security rules. It blocks unauthorised access and suspicious connections while allowing legitimate traffic, and so protects a network from hackers and malware.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(a) Describe the term Multimedia. (1 mark)

(b) Give one advantage and one disadvantage of social media. (2 marks)

(c) State two ethical behavior of proper use of social media. (2 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(a) Multimedia (1 mark).** Multimedia is the **combination of several types of media - text, graphics (images), audio, video and animation - in one digital product**, usually with some interaction from the user (for example an educational website, a computer-based tutorial or a video game).

**(b) Social media (2 marks).**

- *One advantage:* it lets people communicate, share information and keep in touch quickly and cheaply with friends, family and the public anywhere in the world (it is also used for learning, advertising and small business).
- *One disadvantage:* it can be addictive and waste time (reducing study or work), and it exposes users to cyberbullying, false information (fake news) and loss of privacy.

(Any one correct advantage and any one correct disadvantage.)

**(c) Two ethical behaviours in the proper use of social media (2 marks)** (any two):

- Respect other people's privacy: do not post or tag someone's photos or personal information without permission.
- Do not bully, insult or harass others, and do not spread rumours or false information.
- Respect copyright: do not share other people's work without permission or acknowledgement.
- Protect your own personal information and use polite, respectful language.
